observations: Photo 0 shows a white and grey Singer sewing machine on a wooden base. The brand name 'SINGER' is visible on the front panel.
Photo 1 shows the side view of the same machine, revealing a motor attached to the right side, indicating electric operation. The wooden base has some tools and parts inside.
The machine has a handwheel on the right side, suggesting manual operation is also possible.
The motor in photo 1 has a label, but the text is not legible.
The wooden base appears worn, with visible scratches and dust.
No power cord is visible in the photos, though a plug is seen inside the base in photo 1.

claims.claim: Original singer machine both electric and manual
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows the 'SINGER' brand name. Photo 1 shows a motor for electric operation and a handwheel for manual operation, confirming dual functionality.

risks.risk: The machine may not be functional, especially the electric motor.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the machine operating electrically and manually.

risks.risk: The motor may be damaged or incompatible with Nigerian power supply (220V, 50Hz).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the motor label showing voltage and frequency specifications.

risks.risk: The machine may be missing essential parts or accessories.
risks.proof: A photo showing all included accessories and parts laid out, or a video demonstrating full functionality.

proof_requests: A video showing the machine operating both electrically and manually.
A clear photo of the motor label showing voltage and frequency.
A photo of all included accessories and parts.
response.reason: The machine is identifiable as a Singer sewing machine with dual electric and manual operation, but functionality, motor compatibility, and completeness are unverified. Proof is needed to confirm working condition and suitability for Nigerian power supply.
